headline: November seller prep checklist.
subhead: Five concrete maintenance steps to prepare your property before winter buyers walk through. Swipe.

slides.title: Service the heating system.
slides.text: Buyers check furnace age and service tags immediately. Hire a technician to clean, test, and tag the unit.

slides.title: Clear roof and gutters.
slides.text: Fallen leaves trap moisture and cause leaks. Clean gutters and ensure downspouts divert water away from the foundation.

slides.title: Seal exterior draft points.
slides.text: Replace worn weatherstripping around exterior entry doors. Cold drafts during showings make buyers question heating efficiency and insulation.

slides.title: Test ground fault outlets.
slides.text: Test every GFCI receptacle in kitchens, bathrooms, and outside. It takes ten minutes and resolves an easy inspection flag.

slides.title: Gather mechanical service records.
slides.text: Compile receipts for your roof, heating service, and septic pumping. Having invoices organized on the counter builds buyer confidence.

caption:
Cold weather changes what buyers notice during Danbury property showings.

If you plan to sell over the coming months, seasonal prep matters. Buyers touring homes in Danbury CT right now look straight at mechanicals, drafts, and exterior drainage. They check the furnace service tag before they look at paint colors.

Small items like an unserviced boiler or overflowing gutters become easy negotiation points during inspection review. Taking care of these five maintenance items before listing keeps your contract moving forward smoothly.
